items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And he told me that he had a job for me, to get in the union. So I got in the union, I went to work with him at the Three Deuces.

ctx.x: Yes, yes. The first solo I ever had on a recording was with Art, something called Battery Bounce, I believe. We made the Wee Baby Blues and the Battery Bounce and all this. This was the -- it was unamplified guitar, incidentally, all, But, I worked with Art every night for about two years, and he heard me with my mother's trio. He came by the place I was working, and I wasn't even in the union. And he told me that he had a job for me, to get in the union. So I got in the union, I went to work with him at the…

started grasping some of it, or knowing what I had learned after I left -- after he left, you know. And I used to play things that I had -- I tried to play some of the things that I heard him playing, voicings and things like that. And this was a tremendous training for me,--you know, just can you imagine. And then after we got off at night we -- in the morning, rather -- at night. When we got off at 4:00 o'clock in the morning then we'd go to an after hours spot.
